Hi Marta,

Thanks for sending this over and the excerpt. Short answer: batch embed jobs are broken into per-request tokens at ingestion and those token counts flow into the usage ledger; however we apply a windowed aggregation for hourly/session attribution which can affect how bursts show up on an invoice.

Icen from Billing who can pull a per-request trace and give a line-by-line explanation for the dates you called out. We also like to run a quick sampling export of the 2/14-2/16 window and share a CSV with the upstream request ids mapped to our internal request_ids.

If that works Ian schedule a short call for early next week and provide a proforma credit if we see a misattribution.

Hi all,

I pulled the ledger and ran an attribution pass. Summary below:

- Root cause: The embed pipeline spawned ~18 parallel worker sessions for the same parent job on 2028-02-15 03:42:12 UTC. Each worker committed KV cache warmups which produced tokenized telemetry that our hourly apportionment step counted as billable tokens (these warmups are ordinarily deduplicated later, but because the job time straddled the hourly boundary the dedupe window did not collapse the entries).

- Impact: ~1.9M tokens double-counted across the three-day window; invoice variance: +18% on the token/embedding line for Feb.

- VAT handling: VAT was applied at the line-item level based on the final invoice, so the extra tokens were taxed in the Feb invoice jurisdiction (US/California sales tax exemptions do not apply). Because the overage is retroactive to Feb, VAT liability stays on the Feb invoice. We recommend issuing a proforma credit (credit memo) for the overage and reflecting that credit on the March billing cycle so your tax team can reconcile VAT filings.

Next steps acted on:
1) We like to issue a provisional credit for the duplicated tokens: USD 5,670.00 (gross) which will be netted on your March invoice pending your approval.
2) We can provide a tax-team-friendly CSV that shows original_request_id, redwood_request_id, original_timestamp, token_delta, tax_applied (y/n).
3) Engineering will add a 30-minute dedupe extension for hourly windowing to prevent this class of double-counting.

Attachments: redwood_pricing_matrix_v2.pdf (pricing reference), provisional_credit_calc_02-15.xlsx (internal calc)

Let me know if you want the credit processed as a refund instead of a March netting (refund requires accounts-payable workflow).

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Billing Lead, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Hi Marta,

Thanks for your patience while we investigated. Quick summary and proposed customer-facing resolution for FastHealth:

- Finding: A windowing/deduplication edge case produced ~1.9M duplicated tokens between 2028-02-14 and 2028-02-16. Redwood accepts responsibility for the double-count.

- Financial remedy: We propose a provisional credit (credit memo) of USD 5,670.00 to offset the duplicated tokens. We will net the credit against your March invoice, unless AP requests an immediate refund.

- VAT / tax paperwork: Attached is the CSV export tailored for your tax team with per-request mapping and a column showing whether tax was applied. If you need a tax breakdown report (taxable amount by jurisdiction) we can produce that as a follow-up.

- Next steps:
  1) Please confirm you like the credit netted on March invoice or processed as a refund.
  2) If netting, expect the March invoice to include a line item "Provisional credit: duplicated tokens (Feb)" and a DocuSign link for the credit memo acknowledgment: https://app.docusign.com/embeddedSigning?token=abc123-FH1024
  3) Engineering has scheduled the dedupe-window fix for the next release; we will provide a short postmortem when deployed.

IcP to loop in accounts-payable for the refund flow if preferred.

Best regards,
